Do not run git commands that create commits (`git commit`, `git cherry-pick`, `git rebase`, etc.) on this user's behalf, even when earlier in the same session the user asked for "changes" to be made or seemed to authorize it generally. Edit files, explain what needs to happen and why, and stage changes if asked, but leave the actual commit-creating step to the user.

**Why:** In a debugging/restart session on [[cal-diy-issue-11-reschedule-reason]], the user explicitly said "don't commit nothing i will do that you are here for guide" after noticing the assistant had made several commits (including a `git cherry-pick`, which auto-creates a commit) without a clear enough check-in first.

**How to apply:** When a fix or rebuild step is ready, describe the diff and let the user commit it. If a git operation is unavoidable and inherently commit-creating (e.g. cherry-pick to move a specific commit onto a new branch), ask first and be explicit that it will create a commit. This applies specifically to this user/repo; general commit-permission norms elsewhere still apply as usual.

import { RescheduleReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/[REDACTED:generic-password]/enums";

export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(
  setting: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

```text
#11 Require a reason when a booking is rescheduled [OPEN] assignees: julissaehp

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Event types can already force a **cancellation** reason. The `CancellationReasonRequirement` enum (`packages/[REDACTED:generic-password]/schema.[REDACTED:generic-password]:149`) offers `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` / `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, it is stored on `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/[REDACTED:generic-password]/schema.[REDACTED:generic-password]:287`), and it is enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`.

Rescheduling has no equivalent. A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`, `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but it is always optional — `rg -n "requiresRescheduleReason|RescheduleReasonRequirement"` over the repo returns nothing.

So a host who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, even though a reschedule disrupts the same attendee and moves the same calendar. Hosts who run paid or high-demand event types are the ones who feel it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Mirror the cancellation setting for reschedules:

- a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a `requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, with the same four values and the same default posture;
- a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced, sitting next to the cancellation one;
- validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`;
- the reason surfaced wherever the cancellation reason already is.

### User story

As a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.

### Rough scope

### Source

`specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/future-work.md`, which lists "Reschedule reason requirement (same pattern, separate setting)" as work deliberately deferred from that feature.

### Additional context

Intended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: medium`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.

Your PR has three comments. One is a real review from **zach-short** marked **Changes requested**, and two are from bots. The reviewer thinks the UI part is right and says they'd merge once you fix items 1, 3 and 4 below. Before any of that, there's a deadline.

### ⚠️ Urgent: the PR is about to be auto-closed
The stale bot labeled #81 `Stale` after a week without activity. This repo's bot closes stale PRs 14 days after labeling them. That means #81 can be closed as early as tonight (around 10 PM Eastern) and almost certainly will be by tomorrow evening. **Any comment or push from you removes the label.** Something like "Still working on this, addressing review feedback" is enough. If it does get closed, you can reopen it.

### The review, item by item

**1. Don't edit a migration that's already on `main`** (the biggest issue)
Your earlier PR #36 merged the migration `20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require`, which created the column with `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`. #81 edits that same file to `'OPTIONAL_BOTH'`, and that doesn't work, for two reasons:
- **Prisma never runs a migration twice.** It records each applied migration and skips it after that. Every database that already ran #36, such as your teammates' local databases, keeps the old default. Only a brand-new database would get `OPTIONAL_BOTH`. Also, `[REDACTED:generic-password] migrate dev` notices the edited file and asks people to reset their database.
- **Existing rows aren't NULL.** When Postgres adds a column with a default, it writes that default into every existing row. So every existing event type stores `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`. Your fallback `setting ?? OPTIONAL_BOTH` only applies when the value is null, so it never applies to those rows. Hosts would still be forced to give a reason, which is exactly what you were trying to prevent.

This already affects `main` today. The server rejects a host's reschedule request without a reason (`requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`), while the dialog still says "(Optional)".

**Fix:** restore the old file exactly as it is on main:
```
git checkout team/main -- packages/[REDACTED:generic-password]/migrations/20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql
```
Then add a **new** migration folder containing the reviewer's two SQL statements. Its timestamp has to be later than the newest one on main, `20261028120000_…`. The `ALTER … SET DEFAULT` statement covers event types created from now on, and the `UPDATE` fixes the ones that already exist. Keep your `schema.[REDACTED:generic-password]` change.

**Why the `UPDATE` has to be in this PR:** right now nothing on `main` lets anyone set this field. There's no dropdown, and the update API doesn't accept it. So every stored `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` came from the default, not from a host's choice. Once your dropdown ships, a host could pick that value on purpose, and running the same `UPDATE` later would erase their choice.

**2. Explain why your default differs from #11**
#11 asks for "the same default posture" as the cancellation setting, and cancellation defaults to `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`. The reviewer agrees `OPTIONAL_BOTH` is reasonable. They just want the decision and the option you didn't take written in the PR description. No code change is needed. For example: *"Default is `OPTIONAL_BOTH` so existing event types don't suddenly require a reason. I considered `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` to match cancellation as #11 asks, but didn't use it because it would change behavior for every existing event type."*

**3. Merge conflict and `Closes #11`**
After you branched, commit `e7a3bfc42a` ("Implement custom email send time") added a booking-reminder dropdown in the same spot as yours in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx`, right after the cancellation-reason block. Git can't decide which one goes first. The fix is to keep **both** blocks. `common.json` changed on both sides too, but git merges it automatically. Also add `Closes #11` to the description, because the Sprint 1 spec requires it.

**4. Tests**
Your only test change updates an existing test's expected result. The reviewer wants new tests for `RescheduleDialog`:
- When a reason is required and the box is empty, "Request reschedule" is disabled.
- When a reason is required and text is typed, the button is enabled.
- "(Optional)" only shows when no reason is required.

A test that the Advanced tab saves the chosen value would be a bonus. `apps/web/components/dialog/__tests__/EditLocationDialog.test.tsx` is an existing dialog test you can copy the setup from. Also replace the template prompts under "How should this be tested?" with the steps you actually used.

**Minor**
- The Checklist at the bottom still has template lines like "I haven't read the contributing guide" and "My PR is too large." The template expects you to delete the ones that don't apply. Left in, they read as statements about your PR.
- The moved React imports in `RescheduleDialog.tsx` and the re-wrapped line in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` aren't part of the feature. They're fine if Biome made them, so just reply saying that.

**Rubric (out of 10):** correctness 5, tests 4, code quality 7, docs 4, AI transparency 5, overall 4 ("not as-is; yes after items 1, 3 and 4").

40	      // @TODO: notify sentry
41	    },
42	  });
43

56	              {!isReasonRequired && <span className="text-subtle font-normal"> (Optional)</span>}
57	            </p>
58	            <TextArea

60	              name={t("reason_for_reschedule")}
61	              value={rescheduleReason}
62	              onChange={(e) => setRescheduleReason(e.target.value)}
63	              className="mb-5 sm:mb-6"
64	            />
65	          </div>

70	          </Button>

78	              });

80	            {t("send_reschedule_request")}

```typescript
import { RescheduleReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/[REDACTED:generic-password]/enums";
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { RescheduleDialog } from "../RescheduleDialog";

const { mockRequestReschedule } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockRequestReschedule: vi.fn() }));

vi.mock("@calcom/trpc/react", () => ({
  trpc: {
    useUtils: () => ({ viewer: { bookings: { invalidate: vi.fn() } } }),
    viewer: {
      bookings: {
        requestReschedule: {
          useMutation: () => ({ mutate: mockRequestReschedule, isPending: false }),
        },
      },
    },
  },
}));

const BOOKING_UID = "booking-uid";
const REQUIRED_FOR_HOST = [
  RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH,
  RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY,
];

const renderDialog = (requiresRescheduleReason?: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null) =>
  render(
    <RescheduleDialog
      isOpenDialog
      setIsOpenDialog={vi.fn()}
      bookingUid={BOOKING_UID}
      requiresRescheduleReason={requiresRescheduleReason}
    />
  );

const getRequestButton = () => screen.getByTestId("send_request");
const typeReason = (reason: string) =>
  fireEvent.change(screen.getByRole("textbox"), { target: { value: reason } });

describe("RescheduleDialog", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
  });

  describe("when the host must give a reason", () => {
    it.each(REQUIRED_FOR_HOST)("%s: disables the request button until a reason is entered", (requirement) => {
      renderDialog(requirement);
      expect(getRequestButton()).toBeDisabled();

      typeReason("Running late");

      expect(getRequestButton()).toBeEnabled();
    });

    it.each(REQUIRED_FOR_HOST)("%s: does not label the reason as optional", (requirement) => {
      renderDialog(requirement);

      expect(screen.queryByText("(Optional)")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    });

    it("keeps the request button disabled when the reason is only whitespace", () => {
      renderDialog(RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY);

      typeReason("   ");

      expect(getRequestButton()).toBeDisabled();
    });

    it("sends the reason with the reschedule request", () => {
      renderDialog(RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY);

      typeReason("Running late");
      fireEvent.click(getRequestButton());

      expect(mockRequestReschedule).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        bookingUid: BOOKING_UID,
        rescheduleReason: "Running late",
      });
    });
  });

  // Only the host opens this dialog, so an attendee-only requirement leaves the reason optional here.
  describe("when the host does not have to give a reason", () => {
    it.each([
      RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY,
      RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH,
      null,
      undefined,
    ])("%s: labels the reason as optional and allows sending without one", (requirement) => {
      renderDialog(requirement);

      expect(screen.getByText("(Optional)")).toBeInTheDocument();
      expect(getRequestButton()).toBeEnabled();
    });
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 17:52:20Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```markdown
---
name: cal-diy-vitest-test-setup
description: Vitest 4.1 ignores vitest.workspace.ts here, so only packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts runs; apps/web component tests must mock next/navigation and useLocale themselves.
metadata:
  type: project
---

This repo runs Vitest 4.1, which ignores `vitest.workspace.ts`. Every test runs under the root `vitest.config.mts`, whose only setup file is `packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts`. That file provides the jest-dom matchers and a ResizeObserver polyfill. The per-project setups named in the workspace file, such as `packages/ui/components/test-setup.tsx` with its next/navigation, useLocale and useIsPlatform mocks, never run.

**Why:** anything that renders `@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog` throws "invariant expected app router to be mounted" unless the test file mocks `next/navigation`'s `useRouter` itself. `EditLocationDialog.test.tsx` and `RescheduleDialog.test.tsx` both do this.

**How to apply:**
- When writing an `apps/web` component test, mock `next/navigation` (`useRouter`) and `@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale` in the test file.
- Run a single file with `yarn test <path>`. The script sets TZ=UTC, so the command also works in PowerShell.
- To type-check one test file with a temporary tsconfig placed outside the repo, set `typeRoots` to the repo's `node_modules/@types`. Otherwise `@types/jest` and `@types/testing-library__jest-dom` go missing and you get false errors.

```

```text
#78 feat: warn before leaving event edit page with unsaved changes (#9) by zach-short, merged 2026-10-09T02:10:47Z
Closes: 9

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #9

Leaving the event type editor with unsaved edits used to throw them away without a word. Now a click on any link that leaves the editor (the sidebar, the top navigation, or the back arrow in the header) opens a dialog first. "Save" saves and then goes where the user clicked. `Don't save and leave` goes there without saving. Escape or the close button keeps the user on the page with the edits intact. With no edits, or right after a save, links work as before and no dialog appears.

"Has unsaved edits" is the same signal that enables the header Save button, `formMethods.formState.isDirty` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`). Issue #10 (#20) made that signal trustworthy on load, so the dialog and the Save button always agree.

**How it works.** The App Router has no API for blocking a navigation, and the editor's existing `useHandleRouteChange` hook only runs after the pathname has already changed. So the new `useUnsavedChangesGuard` hook listens for link clicks on `document` in the capture phase while the form is dirty. That listener runs before `next/link`'s own handler, which returns early when the event is already `defaultPrevented` (`next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js:319` in Next 16.2.3). The hook stops the click and remembers the destination; the dialog then decides what happens. It lets a click through when the link opens a new tab (Cmd, Ctrl, Shift or middle click, or `target="_blank"`), when it points to another site, and when it stays on the same page. The last case covers the editor's own tabs, which only change `?tabName=` and keep the form state.

"Save" in the dialog runs the same submit path as the header Save button. It resolves to `true` only when the update mutation succeeds. If the server rejects the save, the existing error toast appears and the user stays on the page. If the form is invalid, the user also stays and sees "Error updating settings".

**Two changes outside the editor, both small.**

1. `Shell.tsx`: when `backPath` is a string, the header back arrow is now a real link (`<Button href>`) instead of a button that calls `router.push`. A click listener cannot see where a button is going, so without this the editor could not guard its own back arrow. The destination is unchanged on every page that uses `backPath`. The visible difference is that the arrow can now be middle-clicked into a new tab. `backPath={true}` still calls `router.back()`.
2. Closing or reloading the tab with unsaved edits now shows the browser's own "Leave site?" prompt (`beforeunload`). The browser fixes its wording, and it cannot offer Save.

**Decided with the issue owner (2026-10-07).** The issue's open question, whether the browser Back button should open the dialog, is answered **no**. Next 16 reloads the page on Back for any history entry that lacks its private `__NA` state (`next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:284`), so guarding Back means writing that private state ourselves. That is fragile across Next upgrades, and it belongs in its own issue if anyone wants it.

**Known limits.** Browser Back is not guarded, as above. Navigation started from code rather than from a link, such as the Cmd+K menu, is not guarded either, because it never passes through a link click. Links to other sites fall to the browser's own prompt.

**Files.** New: `apps/web/modules/event-types/hooks/useUnsavedChangesGuard.ts` (+ test), `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/dialogs/UnsavedChangesDialog.tsx` (+ test). Changed: `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (wiring), `Shell.tsx` (back arrow), `en/common.json` (3 strings). 493 lines of code, 301 of them tests.

## Design

**Decision.** While the form has unsaved edits, one capture-phase click listener on `document` stops a same-origin link that leaves the editor and opens the dialog, and a `beforeunload` listener covers closing or reloading the tab.

**Alternatives considered.**

1. Use the editor's existing `useHandleRouteChange` hook. It runs only after the pathname has already changed, so it cannot keep the user on the page.
2. Also guard the browser Back button with a `popstate` listener. Next 16 reloads on Back for any history entry without its private `__NA` state, so this means writing private Next state ourselves, which any Next upgrade can break.
3. Put a guard into each navigation component: the sidebar, the top navigation and the back arrow. These are rendered by the shared `Shell`, so every page would carry editor-only code, and a link added later would not be guarded.

**Rationale.** One listener on `document` sees every link on the page, including links added later. It runs before `next/link`'s own handler, which skips a click that is already `defaultPrevented`, so it needs no private Next API.

**Consequences.** Browser Back and navigation started from code, such as the Cmd+K menu, are not guarded. The header back arrow in `Shell.tsx` had to become a real link so the listener can see where it goes. Links to other sites fall to the browser's own prompt.

After an edit to the title, the Bookings link opens the dialog, and Escape closes it with the edit kept. The header back arrow opens the dialog too, and Save saves and lands on Event Types. The Save button greys out just before the navigation, which is the save completing.

=================== ISSUE #9 [CLOSED] Warn user before leaving event edit page with unsaved changes ===================
## User Story
As an event host, I want a warning before leaving an unsaved event type edit page to prevent accidental data loss.

## User Scenario
A user editing an event type clicks a navigation link before saving. Instead of silently discarding edits, a confirmation dialog appears offering options to "Save" (commits edits, then navigates), "Don't save and leave" (discards edits, navigates), or close the dialog to continue editing.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. If the user has made edits but hasn't saved them, clicking any navigation link (like the sidebar or header) opens a warning dialog instead of immediately leaving the page.
2. If the user has made no edits (or already saved them), clicking a navigation link takes them directly to the new page without showing a warning.
3. If the user clicks "Don't save and leave," their edits are discarded and they are taken to their clicked destination.
4. If the user clicks "Save," the system attempts to save their edits. If successful, they are taken to their clicked destination. If the save fails, they remain on the editing page and see an error message.
5. If the user dismisses the dialog (by pressing Esc or clicking the "×" button), they remain on the editing page with all of their unsaved changes kept intact.

## Out of Scope
- Unsaved-change warnings on pages outside the event type editor.
- Auto-saving or cross-session drafts.

## Open Question
- Should the browser Back button trigger the dialog?

PR #20 fix: stop the description editor marking an untouched event type as changed (#10) by zach-short, merged 2026-09-16T21:03:30Z
Files: apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/EventSetupTab.tsx, apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/description-editor-guard.test.ts, apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/description-editor-guard.ts, packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts

## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #10

Opening an event type for editing left **Save** enabled even though nothing had been touched, and
pressing it wrote a corrupted description back to the database.

The Save button was never the problem. It already guards itself with
`disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`), and that guard works — the
form was genuinely dirty on load.

**Root cause.** The Lexical editor behind the description field calls `setText` twice while it
mounts (measured on a running app: two emissions ~48ms apart, identical), echoing back the value it
was just seeded with. `EventSetupTab` wrote that echo into the form with `{ shouldDirty: true }`.
Because the `md.render` -> `turndown` round-trip is lossy, the echoed value often differs from what
is stored, so react-hook-form correctly concluded the form had changed:

| stored description | value in the form after mount, before this PR |
|---|---|
| `NULL` | `""` |
| `**bold** and _italic_` | `****bold**** and _italic_` |

That second row is the part the issue does not mention: `handleSubmit` builds its payload from
`dirtyValues` (`useEventTypeForm.ts:320`, `:410`), so `description` *was* in the payload. Saving an
event type you had not edited silently doubled the asterisks in its description.

**The fix.** Two changes:

1. `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/description-editor-guard.ts` (new) — a small
   guard that answers one question per emission: is this the user editing, or the editor echoing
   its own seed value? It remembers the first emitted value, treats anything equal to it as an echo,
   and latches on the first differing value so every later emission is an edit. The latch matters:
   without it, clearing the description back to the echoed text would be silently dropped.
2. `useEventTypeForm.ts` — `description: eventType.description ?? undefined` becomes `?? ""`. With
   the default no longer `undefined`, emptying the description of an event type that never had one
   returns the form to genuinely clean rather than leaving it dirty against `undefined`.

**Known limitation, deliberately out of scope.** "Edit the description, then edit it back, and the
button greys out again" is not achievable while the markdown round-trip stays lossy — `- a` / `- b`
comes back as `*   a` / `*   b`, and a hard line break comes back as `<br>`. That lossiness is a
separate defect and deserves its own issue; this PR stops it dirtying an untouched form and stops
it reaching the database on a no-op save.

```cjs
// Read-only experiment: does reverting an edit clear react-hook-form's isDirty in the event-type editor?
// Uses the repo's own react / react-dom / react-hook-form / jsdom (resolved from apps/web) and touches no repo files.
// Mirrors: useEventTypeForm.ts defaultValues (title L44, metadata L100, requiresCancellationReason L137),
// the three Advanced-tab Controllers in EventAdvancedTab.tsx, and EventTypeWebWrapper's post-save form.reset(getValues()).
const path = require("path");
const REPO = "C:/Users/Julissa/CSCI 435Project/cal.diy";
const load = (m) => require(require.resolve(m, { paths: [path.join(REPO, "apps/web")] }));

const { JSDOM } = load("jsdom");
const dom = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><html><body></body></html>");
global.window = dom.window;
global.document = dom.window.document;
global.navigator = dom.window.navigator;
global.HTMLElement = dom.window.HTMLElement;
global.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true;

const React = load("react");
const { createRoot } = load("react-dom/client");
const { act } = load("react-dom/test-utils");
const { useForm, FormProvider, Controller } = load("react-hook-form");
const h = React.createElement;

function run({ label, mountRescheduleDropdown, rescheduleInFormDefaults, storedMetadata }) {
  const stored = {
    title: "Tennis class",
    requiresCancellationReason: "MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY",
    requiresRescheduleReason: "OPTIONAL_BOTH", // every row holds this after the new migration
    metadata: storedMetadata,
  };
  const defaultValues = {
    title: stored.title,
    metadata: stored.metadata,
    requiresCancellationReason: stored.requiresCancellationReason || null,
    ...(rescheduleInFormDefaults
      ? { requiresRescheduleReason: stored.requiresRescheduleReason || null }
      : {}),
  };

  const handles = {};
  let form;
  let openAdvancedTab;
  function Editor() {
    form = useForm({ defaultValues });
    const [advancedOpen, setAdvancedOpen] = React.useState(false);
    openAdvancedTab = () => setAdvancedOpen(true);
    void form.formState.isDirty; // the Save button and the guard read this, which subscribes to it
    return h(
      FormProvider,
      form,
      h(Controller, { name: "title", render: ({ field }) => ((handles.title = field.onChange), null) }),
      advancedOpen &&
        h(Controller, {
          name: "requiresCancellationReason",
          defaultValue: stored.requiresCancellationReason ?? "MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY",
          render: ({ field }) => ((handles.cancellation = field.onChange), null),
        }),
      advancedOpen &&
        mountRescheduleDropdown &&
        h(Controller, {
          name: "requiresRescheduleReason",
          defaultValue: stored.requiresRescheduleReason ?? "OPTIONAL_BOTH",
          render: ({ field }) => ((handles.reschedule = field.onChange), null),
        }),
      advancedOpen &&
        h(Controller, {
          name: "metadata.bookingReminderMinutes",
          render: ({ field }) => ((handles.reminder = field.onChange), null),
        })
    );
  }

  const root = createRoot(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div")));
  const dirty = () => (form.formState.isDirty ? "DIRTY" : "clean");
  const steps = {};
  act(() => root.render(h(Editor)));
  steps["1 page loaded (Setup tab)"] = dirty();
  act(() => openAdvancedTab());
  steps["2 opened Advanced tab, no edits"] = dirty();
  act(() => handles.title("Tennis class (edited)"));
  steps["3 edited the title"] = dirty();
  act(() => handles.title("Tennis class"));
  steps["4 reverted the title"] = dirty();
  if (handles.reschedule) {
    act(() => handles.reschedule("MANDATORY_BOTH"));
    act(() => handles.reschedule("OPTIONAL_BOTH"));
    steps["5 changed + reverted reschedule reason"] = dirty();
  } else {
    steps["5 changed + reverted reschedule reason"] = "n/a";
  }
  act(() => handles.cancellation("MANDATORY_BOTH"));
  act(() => handles.cancellation("MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY"));
  steps["6 changed + reverted cancellation reason"] = dirty();
  act(() => form.reset(form.getValues())); // what EventTypeWebWrapper does after a successful save
  act(() => handles.title("Tennis class (edited)"));
  act(() => handles.title("Tennis class"));
  steps["7 after a save: edited + reverted title"] = dirty();
  act(() => root.unmount());
  return { label, steps };
}

const scenarios = [
  { label: "A main today (no #81)", mountRescheduleDropdown: false, rescheduleInFormDefaults: false, storedMetadata: {} },
  { label: "B main + #81 (current merge)", mountRescheduleDropdown: true, rescheduleInFormDefaults: false, storedMetadata: {} },
  { label: "C main + #81 + 1-line fix", mountRescheduleDropdown: true, rescheduleInFormDefaults: true, storedMetadata: {} },
  { label: "D main, reminder time saved", mountRescheduleDropdown: false, rescheduleInFormDefaults: false, storedMetadata: { bookingReminderMinutes: 60 } },
  { label: "E +#81, reminder time saved", mountRescheduleDropdown: true, rescheduleInFormDefaults: false, storedMetadata: { bookingReminderMinutes: 60 } },
  { label: "F +#81+fix, reminder saved", mountRescheduleDropdown: true, rescheduleInFormDefaults: true, storedMetadata: { bookingReminderMinutes: 60 } },
];

const results = scenarios.map(run);
const stepNames = Object.keys(results[0].steps);
const col = 30;
console.log("step".padEnd(42) + results.map((r) => r.label.slice(0, col - 2).padEnd(col)).join(""));
for (const s of stepNames) {
  console.log(s.padEnd(42) + results.map((r) => String(r.steps[s]).padEnd(col)).join(""));
}

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:39:10Z)**_

Reverting a change should clear the warning; that's how #78 is designed. But the investigation found something bigger, and part of what I told you last time was wrong. In the real editor, **just opening the Advanced tab** marks the form as changed, with no edits at all. Your new field causes that on its own, and `main`'s new reminder dropdown already causes it for most event types.

I changed no repo files; all experiments ran from my scratchpad. I also checked your merge commit `104daab567`: none of your other files went in, and the resolution is what I described.

### 1. What the implementation is designed to do
- **#78's guard only switches on while `form.formState.isDirty` is true** (`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:210`). While on, clicking a link that leaves the editor opens the Save / "Don't save and leave" / stay dialog, and closing the browser tab triggers the browser's own prompt.
- **#78 reuses the Save button's signal on purpose.** Its description defines "has unsaved edits" as "the same signal that enables the header Save button" (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:281`: `disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}`). It also says "with no edits, or right after a save … no dialog appears."
- **`isDirty` compares the whole form against its default values.** Those defaults are built in `useEventTypeForm.ts:42–138`. Change something and change it back, and the values match again, so `isDirty` returns to false. That only works if every field on screen has an entry in the defaults.

### 2. Intentional or bug? Bug.
- **Requirements:** issue #9's acceptance criterion 2 says "no edits, no warning". Issue #10 says Save stays disabled when nothing has changed.
- **Precedent:** PR #20 (by #78's author, who is also your reviewer) changed a default in `useEventTypeForm.ts` specifically so that reverting "returns the form to genuinely clean rather than leaving it dirty against `undefined`". It called the one case it couldn't fix a "known limitation … separate defect".
- **Tests:** #78's tests feed in `hasUnsavedChanges` directly, so nothing treats stuck-dirty as intended.
- **The mechanism** is in react-hook-form 7.43.3, `node_modules/react-hook-form/dist/index.esm.mjs`:
  1. A `Controller` writes its field's value into the form when it mounts, even if the field has no default (`:381–383`, `:1503–1511`).
  2. Every `Controller` also runs `useFormState` (`:377`). Its mount effect re-checks `isDirty` for the **whole form** (`:242–249`), without any user edit.
  3. That check is `!deepEqual({...defaults, ...values}, defaults)` (`:1641`, `:1841–1845`). A field missing from the defaults never matches, so the form becomes dirty the moment that dropdown mounts, and stays dirty after any revert.
  4. The editor renders only the active tab (`EventType.tsx:103`) and loads the Advanced tab on demand (`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:58`). So the Advanced dropdowns always mount after the form exists, and that's when this check takes effect.

**Correction:** last time I said opening the Advanced tab doesn't set off the warning. That was wrong. My first experiment mounted the dropdown at the same time as the form, which the real editor never does. Rerun with the editor's real order:

| Scenario | Open Advanced tab, no edits | Edit, then revert | After a save |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. `main` today | ❌ dirty | ❌ dirty | ✅ clean |
| B. `main` + #81 (your merge) | ❌ dirty | ❌ dirty | ✅ clean |
| C. B + one-line fix | ❌ dirty | ❌ dirty | ✅ clean |
| D. `main`, event type with a saved reminder time | ✅ clean | ✅ clean | ✅ clean |
| E. `main` + #81, saved reminder time | ❌ dirty | ❌ dirty | ✅ clean |
| F. B + fix, saved reminder time | ✅ clean | ✅ clean | ✅ clean |

"After a save" is always clean because the editor resets its defaults to the current values after saving (`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:145`).

### 3. Did #81 introduce an integration problem? Yes, though it isn't the only cause.
- **Yours:** comparing D with E isolates your field. On an event type where `main` behaves correctly, adding your dropdown makes opening the Advanced tab enable Save and switch on the "Unsaved changes" dialog, with no edits.
  - Your dropdown mirrors the cancellation one, but the cancellation field also has a line in the form's defaults (`useEventTypeForm.ts:137`). Your field doesn't, and both #20's Save button and #78's dialog rely on it.
  - E also implies that even before the merge, your branch would bring back issue #10's "Save enabled with no changes". #78 adds the dialog on top.
- **Not yours:** row A shows `main` already has the same bug. The "Reminder email" dropdown (commit `e7a3bfc42a`) uses `metadata.bookingReminderMinutes`, which is missing from the stored settings of any event type that never saved a reminder time. That's most of them, and it's why C is still dirty with your fix.

### 4. Smallest fix
For #81, add one line to `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts`, right after line 137:
```ts
      requiresRescheduleReason: eventType.requiresRescheduleReason || null,
```
- **It mirrors the cancellation field exactly.** Row F shows it clears every case: opening the tab, reverting the title, reverting your dropdown and reverting cancellation.
- **Nothing else needs to change:** not the guard, not the dialog, not your dropdown.
- **Add a test** to the existing `useEventTypeForm.test.ts` checking that the stored value ends up in the form's defaults.
- **It relies on item 1.** After your migration's backfill, every row stores `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, so reverting the dropdown to "Optional for both" matches the default.

I'd report the reminder bug to that feature's owner, or open an issue with this evidence, rather than fix it inside #81. The fix is similar, but it changes how that feature handles its stored settings, so it's their decision. Until it's fixed, event types without a saved reminder time will still show the false warning, with or without your fix.

**Caveat:** I verified this with the repo's exact react-hook-form version and the editor's mount order, not by clicking through the running app. You can confirm it in about 30 seconds: open an event type, change nothing, switch to Advanced, and see whether Save becomes clickable. The experiment script is at `C:\Users\Julissa\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Julissa-CSCI-435Project-cal-diy\fdfddafb-9974-4ccb-be41-6cd000a62bd6\scratchpad\rhf-integration-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri].cjs`; run it with `node` on that path.

Do you want me to make the one-line fix and add the test? You'd commit it separately.

const mockEventType = {
  id: 1,
  title: "Test Event",
  slug: "test-event",
  length: 30,
  metadata: {},
  bookingFields: [],
  locations: [],
  users: [],
  hosts: [],
  children: [],
  hashedLink: [],
  team: null,
  schedulingType: null,
  requiresCancellationReason: CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY,
  requiresRescheduleReason: RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH,
} as unknown as EventTypeSetupProps["eventType"];

function AdvancedTabHarness({ onSubmit }: { onSubmit: (data: EventTypeUpdateInput) => void }) {
  const { form, handleSubmit } = useEventTypeForm({ eventType: mockEventType, onSubmit });

  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Form form={form} handleSubmit={handleSubmit}>
        <EventAdvancedTab
          eventType={mockEventType}
          team={null}
          calendarsQuery={{ data: undefined, isPending: false, error: null }}
          showToast={vi.fn()}
          showBookerLayoutSelector={false}
          orgId={null}
        />
        <button type="submit">Save event type</button>
      </Form>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}

const getRescheduleReasonSetting = () => {
  const setting = screen.getByText("require_reschedule_reason").closest(".border-subtle");
  if (!(setting instanceof HTMLElement)) throw new Error("Require reschedule reason setting not found");
  return setting;
};

const chooseRescheduleReason = (optionLabel: string) => {
  const setting = getRescheduleReasonSetting();
  const select = within(setting).getByRole("combobox");
  select.focus();
  fireEvent.keyDown(select, { key: "ArrowDown", code: "ArrowDown" });
  fireEvent.click(within(setting).getByText(optionLabel));
};

describe("EventAdvancedTab - require reschedule reason", () => {
  it.each([
    ["mandatory_for_both", RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH],
    ["mandatory_for_host_only", RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY],
    ["mandatory_for_attendee_only", RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY],
  ])("saves the %s option as %s when the event type is submitted", async (optionLabel, savedValue) => {
    const onSubmit = vi.fn();
    render(<AdvancedTabHarness onSubmit={onSubmit} />);

    chooseRescheduleReason(optionLabel);
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save event type" }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    const payload = onSubmit.mock.calls[0][0];
    expect(payload).toMatchObject({ id: 1, requiresRescheduleReason: savedValue });
    expect(payload).not.toHaveProperty("requiresCancellationReason");
  });
});

I added the test, it passes, and no production code changed. It covers the reviewer's item 4 suggestion: "a test that the Advanced tab saves the chosen value would also help."

**The change: one new file, nothing else touched**
`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.test.tsx` (111 lines), next to the component.
- **It renders the real `EventAdvancedTab`**, driven by the real `useEventTypeForm` hook and the editor's own `<Form>`, wired the same way as `EventType.tsx:102`. So the test goes through the same path as clicking Save.
- **It picks an option in the real "Require reschedule reason" dropdown,** using the same ArrowDown-then-click technique as `select.test.tsx`. It looks only inside that setting's own box, so the cancellation dropdown's identical option labels can't interfere.
- **It then clicks a submit button and checks what would be sent to the server.** The payload must contain `{ id: 1, requiresRescheduleReason: <chosen value> }` and must **not** contain `requiresCancellationReason`, so only the setting you changed is saved.
- **It covers 3 cases,** the three options that differ from the default. Re-selecting "Optional for both" isn't a change, and the editor doesn't save an unchanged form.
- **It follows existing patterns:**
  - It stubs the 5 heavy, unrelated children that render by default: the calendar selectors (one uses tRPC), `FormBuilder`, `RequiresConfirmationController` and `DisableReschedulingController`. That's how `EventTypeLayout.test.tsx` stubs its heavy children.
  - It mocks `useLocale` like the other tests, and the `as unknown as` fixture matches the existing one.

import dotEnv from "dotenv";
import { exec as execCb } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";

import { isPrismaAvailableCheck } from "./is-[REDACTED:generic-password]-available-check";

dotEnv.config({ path: "../../.env" });

const exec = promisify(execCb);

/**
 * TODO: re-write this when Prisma.io gets a programmatic migration API
 * Thanks to @olalonde for the idea.
 * @see https://github.com/[REDACTED:generic-password]/[REDACTED:generic-password]/issues/4703#issuecomment-1447354363
 */
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS === "1") {
    console.info("SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS set, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) {
    console.info("No DATABASE_URL found, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!process.env.DATABASE_DIRECT_URL) {
    console.info("No DATABASE_DIRECT_URL found, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!(await isPrismaAvailableCheck())) {
    console.info("Prisma can't be initialized, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  // throws an error if migration fails
  const { stdout, stderr } = await exec("yarn [REDACTED:generic-password] migrate deploy", {
    env: {
      ...process.env,
    },
  });
  console.log(stdout);
  console.error(stderr);

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:50:52Z)**_

This check failure is a CI configuration problem in the team repository. It isn't caused by your code, and you can't fix it from your PR. I changed nothing.

**1. What's causing the error**
- **The cause:** lines 16–17 of `.github/workflows/check-[REDACTED:generic-password]-migrations.yml` give the Postgres service container a Docker Hub login:
  ```yaml
  credentials:
    username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}   # line 16, col 21
    password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}      # line 17, col 21
  ```
- **Why they're blank:** `pr.yml` passes secrets along with `secrets: inherit`, but CI-435-SE/cal.diy has **no Actions secrets at all**. The API reports 0 repository secrets and 0 organization secrets. So both values resolve to `''`.
- **What GitHub does with that:** it rejects a service container whose credentials are present but empty. That's the "Unexpected value ''" error, and the job dies in about 2 seconds, before any step runs.
- **Where the file came from:** upstream Cal.diy (commit `463987c02d`, #26897, January 2026). The team's copy is identical to upstream's, where those secrets exist. The team repository never configured them.

**2. Does the same problem exist on `team/main`? Yes.**
- **The workflow file on your branch is byte-identical to `main`'s,** and your PR doesn't change any workflow files.
- **The same job failed the same way, in 2–3 seconds, on every PR that touched Prisma files:** #36 (your backend PR), #77 and #113, all of which merged anyway. #76 didn't touch Prisma, so the job never ran.

**3. Is it related to your PR's changes? No.**
- **Your PR only *triggers* the job.** It runs only when a PR has Prisma changes (`has-[REDACTED:generic-password]-changes`), and your migration counts as one. The failure happens before any of your code is even checked out.
- **The PR can't fix it either.** `pr.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`, which always uses the workflow files from `main`. That's why the error cites `check-[REDACTED:generic-password]-migrations.yml@77a72d644d…`, `main`'s commit at the time. Even editing the workflow in your PR would change nothing.

**4. Who needs to fix it? The repository maintainers, not you.**
- **You can't change repository secrets.** You have `push` access but not `admin`.
- **Any fix must land in `main`** to take effect.
- **The maintainers have two options:**
  - **Add the secrets.** `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` are needed, and also `CI_DATABASE_URL`: line 6 feeds it into `--shadow-database-url`. Fixing only the credentials would just move the failure to that step.
  - **Or simplify the workflow on `main`.** Remove the `credentials` block (public images like `[REDACTED:generic-password]:18` pull fine without a login) and point the shadow database at the service container directly.
- **The same credentials block is in the e2e workflows** (`e2e-api-v2.yml`, `e2e-app-store.yml`). They'd fail the same way if they ran.

For your PR, the reviewer already called this check "not caused by this PR", so no action is needed. A one-line note in your PR description pointing to #36, #77 and #113 would make that explicit.

This check exists to confirm that the migrations match `schema.[REDACTED:generic-password]`. My earlier evidence covers most of that for your change: Prisma's own schema diff produced exactly your `ALTER` statement, and the throwaway database ended "up to date". If you want the exact CI check, I can run its command locally against a throwaway shadow database with your approval; that does apply migrations, to the shadow database only. I can also draft an issue or comment for the maintainers.
